Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 78 (Windstream missing-address campaign): added operator level company history and its August 2025 Uniti Group merger, corroborated independently via a redirected former Windstream URL now carrying a Uniti Group copyright. No address source succeeded for this Durham row despite further attempts, so none was applied.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Windstream traces to Valor Telecom, established in 2000 to acquire GTE Southwest assets divested by Verizon, and to Windstream Corporation itself, formed in 2006 through a spinoff of Alltels landline business merged with Valor. The company expanded through a long series of acquisitions, including CT Communications for 585 million dollars in 2007, D and E Communications for 330 million dollars in 2009, Iowa Telecom for 1.1 billion dollars and NuVox in 2010, Q-Comm for 782 million dollars in 2010, Hosted Solutions for 310 million dollars also in 2010, PAETEC in 2011, EarthLink for 1.1 billion dollars in 2017, and Broadview Networks for 227 million dollars in 2017. Per Wikipedia, a 2019 US District Court ruling found the company had defaulted on bond payments, its stock fell sharply, and it filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy following a 310 million dollar judgment, emerging in 2020 as a privately held company with debt reduced by more than 4 billion dollars. Wikipedia further states that on August 1, 2025 Uniti Group Inc. completed a merger with Windstream, making Windstream a subsidiary of Uniti. This session independently corroborated that relationship: Windstreams own former business grade colocation web address now redirects to a Uniti Group solutions site carrying a 2026 Uniti Group Inc. copyright notice and routing Windstream branded account logins through it, evidence of a genuine current corporate relationship rather than a stale Wikipedia claim. Given the operating brand itself, Windstream and its consumer facing Kinetic brand, appears to continue rather than being retired, this session records Uniti Group as parent company context rather than correcting the operator field. This specific row sits in Durham, North Carolina. An earlier pass on file for this row found that the Windstream Holdings company history confirms a 2010 acquisition of Hosted Solutions, which had datacenters in Cary, Raleigh, and Charlotte, North Carolina plus Boston, but does not specifically name a Durham facility. This session made a further attempt, searching a data center industry aggregator directorys listing of Durham area facilities, which named several other operators but no facility under Windstream or Hosted Solutions, guessing a dedicated aggregator listing URL, which returned a not found error, and reverse geocoding this rows own coordinates through a third party service twice, both attempts throttled. Given no address source succeeded, none is applied.
